newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open little changed.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open little changed.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open little changed Wednesday, traders said.

Traders were at odds on whether the market would follow through on Tuesday's steep run-up or head lower this morning on profit taking after London robusta futures failed to make their $100 higher pre-opening call.
LIFFE coffee was broadly higher in switch dominated trade. At the midday break, September was $60 higher at $1,565 a tonne, traded $1,570 to $1,548. November was up the same at $1,555.

Tuesday, New York arabica prices ended sharply higher, led by gains in September, on speculative and trade buying amid concerns of a shortage of exchange-certified coffee for delivery against the September contract.
CSCE September settled up 10.25 cents at 169.10 cents a lb after ranging from 170.50 to 158.00 cents. Second-position December rose 5.00 to 151.25, while the back months closed 4.00 to 6.00 higher.
The September/December switch, a barometer of nearby availability, ballooned to 17.35 cents compared with 12.90 cents at the close on Monday.
After Tuesday's close, CSCE reported that certified coffee inventories rose by 382 60-kg bags as of July 21, to 87,231 bags. An additional 4,859 bags were pending grading, the exchange said.
Technically, traders said September would run into some resistance at Tuesday's high of 170.50, with the next level near 173.60 cents. September support was seen near 165.00 cents.

On the weather front, U.S.-based forecaster Weather Services Corp said on Wednesday that there is no damaging cold weather expected during the next seven days in Brazil's coffee belt, with low temperatures forecast mostly in the 50s (low to middle teens C).
